abstract.t: HTTP transfers the state of a resource once, and leaves programmers to keep it up to date as it changes. Braid-HTTP extends HTTP from *transferring* state to *synchronizing* it, with a set of independent extensions, each of which addresses a limitation of HTTP on its own. When used together, a website can synchronize with any other website's state by its URL, just as a page on today's web can link to any other page. This document introduces the extensions, shows how they work alone and together, and points to the documents that define them.
